To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cerebellar granular layer can be regarded as a dynamic population of neurons that can represent the passage‐of time (POT) and that this representation is based on the long‐term integration of inputs by N‐methyl D‐aspartate channels and recurrent connections between granular and Golgi cells.
the cerebellar granular layer is a recurrent spiking neural network that can represent the passage‐of time.

a spiking network model with long‐temporal integration and random recurrent connections can represent the passage of time between the conditioned and unconditioning stimulus onsets in delay eyeblink conditioning; and the glomerulus structure and long‐term potentiation at mossy fibre–granule cell synapses serve to make the representation robust against input noise.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the computational mechanisms of the timing function in the cerebellar network.
the cerebellar mechanisms underlying time perception and time‐to‐response learning.
a spiking neural network model for the passage-of-time representation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cerebellar timing mechanisms are based on a combination of long‐term potentiation and recurrent connections in the granular and molecular layers, which is supported by the present study.
the cerebellum is an essential part of the brain that is capable of generating a representation of the POT, and that the cerebellar granular layer is a neural substrate for the representation.
the cerebellar granular layer is an associative memory that represents the time‐dependent association between the CS and the US.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cerebellum has the computational capacity to represent a time interval between events.
the cerebellum has a recurrent network structure that can represent a dynamic passage‐of‐ time.
the cerebellum can represent the POT by using the temporal structure of its recurrent network.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a dynamic population of granule cells can represent the passage of time, which is a key feature of the cerebellar timing mechanisms.
a dynamic population of granule cells, which is generated by recurrent network dynamics, can serve as a temporal representation.
a recurrent network of spiking neurons can represent the passage‐of time.
